1	import { createClient } from "@/lib/supabase/server";
2	import type { LookDraft, WeatherPayload } from "@/lib/generator/types";

4	/**
5	 * The cache read for "Style an outfit with this".
6	 *
7	 * `outfits_styled_unique (user_id, styled_item_id, generated_on, styled_index)`
8	 * scopes the set to one piece per local day, so this is the whole cache: a hit
9	 * costs one indexed lookup and NO model call.
10	 *
11	 * Ordered by `styled_index`, which is the set's own ordinal — NOT `look_index`,
12	 * which styled rows keep NULL so they cannot collide with the daily drop's
13	 * unique index. `nullsFirst` so a row written before the set existed (index
14	 * NULL) still reads as the first look rather than vanishing off the end.
15	 */
16	export async function loadStyledLooks(
17	  userId: string,
18	  itemId: string,
19	  generatedOn: string,
20	): Promise<string[]> {
21	  const supabase = await createClient();
22	  const { data } = await supabase
23	    .from("outfits")
24	    .select("id, styled_index")
25	    .eq("user_id", userId)
26	    .eq("styled_item_id", itemId)
27	    .eq("generated_on", generatedOn)
28	    .order("styled_index", { ascending: true, nullsFirst: true });
29	  return (data ?? []).map((r) => r.id);
30	}
31	
32	/**
33	 * Which pieces the user has already been shown for this styling today.
34	 *
35	 * Feeds `Ctx.recentlyShown` on a "try another", so the next set sinks what was
36	 * just rejected instead of returning it again — the PR #15 bug, in the styled
37	 * path. A soft penalty, never a filter.
38	 */
39	export async function loadStyledPieceIds(
40	  userId: string,
41	  itemId: string,
42	  generatedOn: string,
43	): Promise<string[]> {
44	  const ids = await loadStyledLooks(userId, itemId, generatedOn);
45	  if (!ids.length) return [];
46	  const supabase = await createClient();
47	  const { data } = await supabase.from("outfit_items").select("item_id").in("outfit_id", ids);
48	  return (data ?? []).map((r) => r.item_id);
49	}
50	
51	/**
52	 * Drop a piece's styled set for the day.
53	 *
54	 * Delete-then-insert, for the same reason `saveDailyLooks` does it: a fresh run
55	 * may return a different number of looks, and leftovers must not survive beside
56	 * the new set. `outfit_items` first — the rows hang off `outfits`.
57	 */
58	export async function clearStyledLooks(
59	  userId: string,
60	  itemId: string,
61	  generatedOn: string,
62	): Promise<void> {
63	  const supabase = await createClient();
64	  const ids = await loadStyledLooks(userId, itemId, generatedOn);
65	  if (!ids.length) return;
66	  await supabase.from("outfit_items").delete().in("outfit_id", ids);
67	  await supabase.from("outfits").delete().in("id", ids);
68	}
69	
70	/**
71	 * Persist a styled SET and return the ids, in order.
72	 *
73	 * `look_index` is deliberately left NULL: `outfits_daily_unique` covers
74	 * (user_id, occasion, generated_on, look_index), and Postgres treats NULLs as
75	 * distinct, so two pieces styled on the same day for the same occasion cannot
76	 * collide. The set's own order lives in `styled_index`.
77	 * `loadDailyLooks`/`saveDailyLooks` filter these rows out entirely.
78	 */
79	export async function saveStyledLooks(
80	  userId: string,
81	  itemId: string,
82	  occasion: string,
83	  generatedOn: string,
84	  weather: WeatherPayload,
85	  looks: LookDraft[],
86	): Promise<string[]> {
87	  const ids: string[] = [];
88	  for (const [i, look] of looks.entries()) {
89	    const id = await saveOne(userId, itemId, occasion, generatedOn, weather, look, i);
90	    if (id) ids.push(id);
91	  }
92	  return ids;
93	}

95	async function saveOne(
96	  userId: string,
97	  itemId: string,
98	  occasion: string,
99	  generatedOn: string,
100	  weather: WeatherPayload,
101	  look: LookDraft,
102	  styledIndex: number,
103	): Promise<string | null> {
104	  const supabase = await createClient();
105	
106	  const { data: row } = await supabase
107	    .from("outfits")
108	    .insert({
109	      user_id: userId,
110	      occasion,
111	      generated_on: generatedOn,
112	      styled_item_id: itemId,
113	      styled_index: styledIndex,
114	      look_name: look.name,
115	      ai_reasoning: look.why,
116	      weather_snapshot: weather,
117	      layout: {
118	        anchorIndex: look.anchorIndex,
119	        pieces: look.pieces.map((p) => ({ itemId: p.itemId, slot: p.slot })),
120	      },
121	    })
122	    .select("id")
123	    .single();
124	  if (!row) return null;
125	
126	  const links = look.pieces.map((p) => ({
127	    outfit_id: row.id,
128	    item_id: p.itemId,
129	    slot: p.category,
130	  }));
131	  if (links.length) await supabase.from("outfit_items").insert(links);
132	
133	  return row.id;
134	}

3	/**
4	 * How many looks one styling returns.
5	 *
6	 * TWO, not three. One re-rank call returns both — `rerank` already takes
7	 * `want` — so the cost is unchanged, and two is enough to feel like a choice
8	 * without implying this screen is a second daily drop. The drop is three
9	 * because its index tabs are drawn for 01/02/03; this is a different question
10	 * with a different answer.
11	 *
12	 * Lives here rather than beside the action because a "use server" file may only
13	 * export async functions — a constant there fails the production build, though
14	 * not the test run.
15	 */
16	export const STYLED_LOOKS = 2;
17	
18	/**
19	 * "Style an outfit with this" — the pure parts.
20	 *
21	 * Deliberately free of any Supabase import so it stays testable under jsdom;
22	 * the persistence lives in `styled-store.ts`.
23	 */
24	
25	/**
26	 * Narrow a ranked candidate list to the combos containing one piece.
27	 *
28	 * This is the whole of "pin the item": the generator already builds every valid
29	 * combination and ranks it, so styling around a chosen piece is a filter over
30	 * that work, not a second algorithm. Order is preserved, so the best combo
31	 * containing the piece stays the best.
32	 *
33	 * Returns empty when the piece fits nothing under the current band — the caller
34	 * widens the formality band and tries again rather than treating that as an
35	 * error, the same "a hard filter must never empty a required slot" rule the
36	 * generator already follows.
37	 */
38	export function pinItem<T extends { items: { id: string }[] }>(combos: T[], itemId: string): T[] {
39	  return combos.filter((c) => c.items.some((i) => i.id === itemId));
40	}
41	
42	/**
43	 * The name to fall back to when the model does not supply one.
44	 *
45	 * A look with no name renders a blank headline on both the detail screen and
46	 * the index tabs, so there is always a name — built from the piece the look was
47	 * styled around, which is also the honest description of it.
48	 */
49	export function styledLookName(item: {
50	  name: string | null;
51	  subcategory: string | null;
52	  category: string;
53	}): string {
54	  return `Around the ${item.name ?? item.subcategory ?? item.category}`;
55	}
56	
57	/**
58	 * The shortlist handed to the re-ranker for a styled look.
59	 *
60	 * The daily path calls `diversify` before the model sees anything; this path
61	 * shipped with `pinned.slice(0, 20)` and never got it. Ranking CLUSTERS — a
62	 * neutral top harmonises with everything, so the raw top of a pinned list is
63	 * near-identical and the model ends up choosing between twenty variations of
64	 * one idea, then returning the safest.
65	 *
66	 * Same reasoning that produced `lib/generator/diversity.ts` in PR #14/#15,
67	 * applied to the second consumer. `diversify` TIERS rather than filters, so
68	 * nothing is discarded and a closet too small to diversify still yields every
69	 * candidate — the collapse PR #15 fixed on the daily path cannot reappear here.
70	 *
71	 * It only reorders a list `pinItem` already filtered, so every combo still
72	 * contains the pinned piece.
73	 */
74	export function shortlistFor<T extends { items: { id: string; category: string }[]; score: number }>(
75	  pinned: T[],
76	  n = 20,
77	): T[] {
78	  return diversify(pinned, n);
79	}

3	-- `outfits_styled_unique (user_id, styled_item_id, generated_on)` allowed exactly
4	-- one row per piece per local day, which is what bounded a styling to a single
5	-- look. Widening it needs an ordinal.
6	--
7	-- ⚠️ That ordinal is NOT `look_index`, and this is the trap worth reading.
8	-- Styled rows keep `look_index` NULL on purpose: `outfits_daily_unique` covers
9	-- (user_id, occasion, generated_on, look_index), and Postgres treats NULLs as
10	-- distinct, which is the only reason a styled look and the day's drop can share
11	-- an occasion without colliding. Giving styled rows a real `look_index` would
12	-- reintroduce that collision — a styled look at index 0 for `work` today would
13	-- clash with the drop's look 0. So the order lives in its own column.

20	  where styled_item_id is not null and styled_index is null;

25	  on public.outfits (user_id, styled_item_id, generated_on, styled_index)

1	import {
2	  currentEntitlements,
3	  regeneratesUsedToday,
4	  recordGeneration,
5	  checkGeneration,
6	  type GenerationKind,
7	} from "@/lib/billing/entitlements";
8	import { QuotaExceededError } from "@/lib/billing/errors";
9	
10	// Re-exported so the generator's call sites keep importing their gate and its
11	// error from one place. The class itself lives in `lib/billing/errors`, which
12	// carries no `server-only` — tests and any future client-side display of the
13	// remaining allowance must be able to reference it.
14	export { QuotaExceededError } from "@/lib/billing/errors";
15	
16	/**
17	 * What the GATE needs to know.
18	 *
19	 * The reroll allowance is a single daily pool across all occasions, so the gate
20	 * needs only the date. `occasion` rides along for the ledger, and is optional
21	 * because the styled action resolves its occasion only AFTER this gate —
22	 * deliberately, so a free user is turned away before we pay for a forecast
23	 * fetch they will never see.
24	 */
25	export type GenerationCheckRequest = {
26	  kind: GenerationKind;
27	  /** Recorded, not used by the check. */
28	  occasion?: string;
29	  /** The user's LOCAL date — never the server's. */
30	  today: string;
31	};
32	
33	/** What the LEDGER needs. `generation_events.occasion` is NOT NULL. */
34	export type GenerationRequest = GenerationCheckRequest & { occasion: string };
35	
36	/**
37	 * The single gate every real generation passes through.
38	 *
39	 * It was written as a deliberate no-op so that adding a paid tier later would be
40	 * a change to THIS file rather than surgery across the generate action. This is
41	 * that change: the decision now lives in `lib/billing`, and this stays the one
42	 * call site the generator knows about.
43	 *
44	 * The three kinds are metered differently (docs/MONETISATION.md §2):
45	 *   drop       — always free, on every tier. The daily drop is never rationed.
46	 *   regenerate — free gets three a day, pooled across every occasion.
47	 *   styled     — Pro only.
48	 */
49	export async function assertCanGenerate(
50	  _userId: string,
51	  req: GenerationCheckRequest,
52	): Promise<void> {
53	  const e = await currentEntitlements();
54	
55	  // Only a reroll needs the counter, so drops and styled looks skip the query
56	  // rather than paying for an answer that cannot change the outcome.
57	  const regeneratesUsed =
58	    req.kind === "regenerate" ? await regeneratesUsedToday(req.today) : 0;
59	
60	  const check = checkGeneration(e, { kind: req.kind, regeneratesUsed });
61	  if (!check.allowed) throw new QuotaExceededError(check.reason);
62	}
63	
64	/**
65	 * Record a generation that actually happened.
66	 *
67	 * Deliberately separate from the check, and called only AFTER the model request
68	 * succeeds: a failed generation costs the user nothing, so charging for one
69	 * would be charging for our own error.
70	 */
71	export async function noteGeneration(userId: string, req: GenerationRequest): Promise<void> {
72	  await recordGeneration(userId, req.occasion, req.today, req.kind);
73	}

I've read every changed file in full. Let me summarize what I checked and why nothing survives as a security finding.

**Files read in full**: style-actions.ts, style-cta.tsx, styled.ts, styled-store.ts, style-cta.test.tsx, migration SQL. Plus `lib/supabase/server.ts`, `lib/outfits/quota.ts`, `lib/billing/entitlements.ts`, and the outfits RLS migration to verify trust boundaries.

**Trust model verified**
- `createClient()` uses the SSR anon key with the user's cookies → RLS applies to every query.
- `outfits`/`outfit_items` have `for all using ((select auth.uid()) = user_id)` (and the equivalent EXISTS predicate for outfit_items). So `.in("id", ids)` / `.in("outfit_id", ids)` in `clearStyledLooks` and `loadStyledPieceIds` cannot reach another tenant, even though they omit an explicit `user_id` filter — the `ids` themselves are already scoped by the earlier `loadStyledLooks` call which does `.eq("user_id", userId)`.

**Attacker-controlled `regenerate` bit** (from Next.js server-action arg): only wired to (a) skip the cache read, (b) load own recentlyShown, (c) call `clearStyledLooks(user.id, itemId, today)`. Every subsequent write still lands under the caller's own RLS scope. Regenerate goes through `assertCanGenerate({kind: "styled"})`, which is Pro-only — free users are blocked before any LLM/weather I/O. Pro users have no per-day styled cap by design (documented in quota.ts), so unlimited "try another" for Pro is authorized behavior, not a defect.

**Save/delete path**: `saveOne` inserts with `user_id: userId` (RLS `with check`) and `outfit_items` links are built from `byId`, which was hydrated from `.eq("user_id", user.id)` — no cross-tenant item_id injection is reachable through the server action's inputs (`itemId` only). `styled_index` is a smallint set by the server loop, not user input.

**Migration**: partial unique index on `(user_id, styled_item_id, generated_on, styled_index) where styled_item_id is not null`, backfill sets existing rows to 0. No FK/trigger/constraint drop with referential-integrity impact; no policy change.

**Parser/validator differentials**: nothing new — no regex/URL/allowlist added.

**Sensitive-to-observability**: `console.error("[styleWithItem] failed:", e)` and `message: e.message` return-to-client are pre-existing (not `+` lines).

**Sibling-path gate parity**: cache-hit skipping quota is by design (Decision 5, "re-opening an answer you already have"), and it can only return rows the user already legitimately owns via RLS.

No security-relevant defect found in the `+` lines.
